title: Translation pilot for >=1 set under a separate high-risk translation gate
context: QPL sets are built translation-ready (structured YAML, machine-readable questions, no idiomatic English) but not translated in v0.1. M3 pilots the first translation under a separate high-risk review gate, reusing the vital-info-translations review model: a qualified medical-translation reviewer (not just a bilingual speaker) plus back-translation QA for any sensitive content (prognosis, end-of-life), plus the original clinician endorsing meaning preservation. The disclaimer and support resources must be localized and verified for the target region. Without back-translation for sensitive content, a subtle meaning shift could cause a patient harm.
objective: Produce a pilot translation of at least one dual-signed-off, adopted QPL set into a target language agreed with the partner, passing the high-risk translation gate: qualified medical-translation reviewer, back-translation QA for sensitive content, original clinician endorsement of meaning preservation, localized disclaimer and regionally-verified support resources.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one QPL set (already dual-signed-off and adopted) is translated into one agreed target language; the translated file is present in sets/<stage>/<topic>/set.<lang-code>.yaml (or an agreed localization directory structure)

The translation was produced or reviewed by a qualified medical-translation reviewer (credentials: medical translation background + familiarity with oncology terminology); reviewer credentials and COI declaration recorded in the review block

Back-translation QA has been performed for any question with a sensitivity field (prognosis, end-of-life, fertility, genetics): a different qualified translator back-translated the target-language text to English; any meaning drift is adjudicated and resolved before sign-off
The original set's clinician reviewer (or an equivalent credentialed clinician) has endorsed that the translated questions preserve the intended meaning and remain clinically appropriate
The verbatim disclaimer is localized (translated and verified to convey the same meaning: 'This is education, not medical advice — always consult your own care team')
Support resources are localized: the resources listed in the translated set are verified support lines in the target region and language, not the English-region resources from the original
The localized support resources have been independently verified current (verifiedBy, verifiedDate) for the target region
CI structural checks pass for the translated file (schema validation; disclaimer, sign-off, provenance, support resources present)
resources: PLAN.md (M3 translation gate; vital-info-translations review model; Data/licensing — CC BY 4.0 permits translation with attribution)
sets/<stage>/<topic>/set.yaml (source set to translate — must be adopted first per qpl-delivery-001)
support/resources.yaml (qpl-support-001 — to identify which resources need regional replacement)
docs/partner-brief.md (qpl-partner-001 — target language/region may be partner-specified)
output: sets/<stage>/<topic>/set.<lang-code>.yaml (translated set with localized disclaimer, localized support resources, and translation review sign-off block)
